specs.title: Discount at checkout
sources: Owner request: "Add a discount to checkout."
Current checkout behaviour (prices and totals as computed today)
in_scope: Checkout can apply a discount to an order and show the reduced total to the buyer
non_goals: Other offers or promotions beyond the one discount (their combination is an open question)

criteria.text: Given an order that qualifies for the discount (eligibility per Q2), when the buyer reaches checkout, then the discount of the size set by Q1 is shown as a separate line and the total equals the pre-discount total minus that discount. BLOCKED by Q1, Q2.
criteria.check: Test to write: checkout total computation for a qualifying order, expected total per the answer to Q1.

criteria.text: Given an order that does not qualify, when the buyer reaches checkout, then no discount line appears and the total is unchanged from today. BLOCKED by Q2.
criteria.check: Negative test: non-qualifying order, total equals the current total.

criteria.text: Given an order that also qualifies for another offer, when the buyer reaches checkout, then the discounts are combined or not as decided in Q3. BLOCKED by Q3.
criteria.check: Test to write: order with the discount and another offer, expected total per the answer to Q3.

criteria.text: Given the discount would make the total negative, when checkout computes the total, then the behaviour decided in Q4 applies. BLOCKED by Q4.
criteria.check: Negative test: discount larger than the order value.

open_questions.question: How large is the discount?

options.changes: Needs a rule for orders below that amount (Q4)

open_questions.waiting_for: owner (price decision; binding allows no provisional choice)

open_questions.question: Who gets the discount?

options.changes: Adds code entry and invalid-code failure path
Adds an eligibility rule and its negative test

open_questions.question: Does it combine with other offers?

options.changes: Totals stack; order of application must be stated

options.option: Does not combine; the larger applies
Does not combine; this one is refused when another applies

open_questions.question: What happens when the discount exceeds the order value?

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version; draft, all criteria blocked on price questions.

actions_now: Write the spec as a draft with every price-dependent criterion blocked and the size, eligibility and combination questions in Open questions, without picking any; escalate to the owner, since prices are money and the binding allows no provisional choice, and hold the implementation line until answered.

Do not edit the approved v1 and do not tell the implementer to just drop the column; put a question to the owner with the options (drop email from criterion 3 in a v2, widen this line to add emails to the reports API, or split emails into a separate line), noting that exporting customer emails is a privacy decision. Once answered, write version 2 with what changed and why, status draft until the owner approves; criterion 3 waits, the other criteria may proceed.

specs.title: User settings kept across devices
sources: Owner request: "Add a user_preferences table with theme and language columns, so users keep their settings across devices." (the table is a design suggestion passed to the architect, not a requirement)
Current behaviour of theme and language settings
in_scope: A signed-in user's theme and language settings follow them to every device they sign in on
non_goals: How or where the settings are stored (architect's decision; the requested table is recorded as a suggestion)
Settings other than theme and language

criteria.text: Given a signed-in user changes their theme on device A, when they sign in on device B, then device B shows the chosen theme.
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions of the same user; manual step: change theme in one browser, sign in from another, expect the same theme.

criteria.text: Given a signed-in user changes their language on device A, when they sign in on device B, then device B shows the interface in the chosen language.
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions of the same user.

criteria.text: Given a user who has never changed a setting, when they sign in on any device, then they see the defaults decided in Q1.
criteria.check: Test to write: new user, expected defaults per Q1. BLOCKED by Q1.

criteria.text: Given two users, when one changes a setting, then the other's settings are unchanged.
criteria.check: Negative test: user isolation.

criteria.text: Given the saved settings cannot be loaded, when the user signs in, then the behaviour decided in Q2 applies and the app still loads.
criteria.check: Negative test with the settings source failing. BLOCKED by Q2.

open_questions.question: What are the defaults for a user with no saved settings?

options.changes: No visible change for new users
Defaults differ per device until the user chooses

open_questions.question: What happens when the saved settings cannot be loaded?

options.changes: User may briefly see wrong theme/language

options.option: Fall back to the device's last local value

open_questions.question: Should settings chosen while signed out carry into the account on sign-in?

options.changes: Adds a merge rule and its criterion

actions_now: Write the spec in terms of behaviour (settings follow the user across devices) and keep the table and columns out of it, recording them only as the owner's design suggestion for the architect; put defaults and failure behaviour in Open questions and leave the spec draft for the owner's approval.

Ask the owner in chat what should happen above 100,000 rows, with options and what each changes (refuse with a clear message and a hint to narrow the filter; generate in the background and deliver a link when ready; split into several files; stream with no limit), without picking one. On the answer, write version 3 with a new numbered criterion and its negative test, what changed and why, status draft until the owner approves, and have work built on v2 checked against v3.

specs.title: Export reports as CSV
sources: Owner request: "Let users export reports as CSV."
Current reports page: table with columns Date, Region, Orders, Revenue; filter by date range
in_scope: A user on the reports page can download the table they see as a CSV file
non_goals: New columns or filters on the reports page

criteria.text: Given the reports page shows the table, when the user chooses Export CSV, then a CSV file downloads whose header row is Date, Region, Orders, Revenue in that order.
criteria.check: Test to write: export endpoint/flow returns a file with that header; manual step: click export, open the file, expect the four headers.

criteria.text: Given the table is filtered to a date range, when the user exports, then the file contains exactly the rows the filtered table contains, with the same values.
criteria.check: Test to write: seeded data, filter applied, compare exported rows to table rows.

criteria.text: Given no filter is applied, when the user exports, then the file contains every row the unfiltered table contains.
criteria.check: Test to write: unfiltered export equals unfiltered table rows.

criteria.text: Given the filter matches no rows, when the user exports, then the behaviour decided in Q1 applies.
criteria.check: Negative test: empty result. BLOCKED by Q1.

criteria.text: Given a value contains a comma, quote or newline, when it is exported, then the file is still valid CSV and opens with the same value.
criteria.check: Test to write: round-trip parse of an exported file with such values.

criteria.text: Given the export would exceed the limit decided in Q2, when the user exports, then the behaviour decided in Q2 applies.
criteria.check: Negative test at the limit. BLOCKED by Q2.

criteria.text: Given a user who may not view the reports page, when they request the export directly, then it is refused as the page is refused today.
criteria.check: Negative test: unauthorized request to the export returns the same refusal as the page.

open_questions.question: What does an export with no matching rows produce?

options.option: A file with the header row only
No file; a message that there is nothing to export
options.changes: Export button disabled or message shown

open_questions.question: Is there a maximum export size, and what happens above it?

options.option: A row limit with a message to narrow the filter
options.changes: Adds a limit value and its message

open_questions.question: How are dates and revenue formatted in the file (locale, currency symbol, decimal separator), and what encoding is used?

options.changes: File matches the screen, may be harder to compute with
Better for spreadsheets; differs from the screen

actions_now: Write the draft spec from the template, with criteria traced to the request and the page's current columns and filter, failure paths included, and the empty-result, size-limit and formatting choices left as open questions. Send it to the owner for answers and approval; the criteria that do not depend on the questions can go ahead.

Leave product-spec at intake: the request already states numbered, testable acceptance criteria, each with a check, so no spec is written and the request goes on to the architect/implementer as its spec. If the factory wants it, note that the security-related details it leaves silent (for example what counts per IP behind a shared proxy, whether successes reset the count) go to the owner as questions rather than being filled in by the product role.

Do not write a spec: this is a bug fix with a known cause and an expected behaviour already defined by the current page, so product-spec does not apply; hand it back to the factory for the implementer, with the existing page behaviour (minus the image) as the reference for the regression test.

specs.title: Colleagues' last online time
sources: Request from a team lead, passed on by the owner without comment: "Show each user when their colleagues were last online."
in_scope: A user can see when each colleague was last online, subject to the visibility, opt-out and retention rules decided in Q1-Q3
non_goals: Showing anything beyond the last-online time

criteria.text: Given a user permitted by Q1 to see a colleague, when they open the colleague's profile or list, then they see the colleague's last-online time. BLOCKED by Q1.
criteria.check: Test to write: permitted viewer sees the time.

criteria.text: Given a user not permitted by Q1 to see a colleague, when they open that colleague's profile or list, or request the data directly, then no last-online time is shown or returned. BLOCKED by Q1.
criteria.check: Negative test: unpermitted viewer, UI and direct request.

criteria.text: Given a colleague who has hidden their status (if allowed by Q2), when anyone views them, then no last-online time is shown. BLOCKED by Q2.
criteria.check: Negative test: hidden user's time is never returned.

criteria.text: Given a last-online record older than the retention decided in Q3, when retention runs, then the record is no longer stored or shown. BLOCKED by Q3.
criteria.check: Test to write with a mocked clock: record past retention is removed.

criteria.text: Given a colleague who has never been online, when a permitted user views them, then the page shows the empty state decided with Q1 rather than a wrong time.
criteria.check: Test to write: never-online user. BLOCKED by Q1.

open_questions.question: Who may see a user's last-online time?

options.option: Only members of the same team

options.changes: Monitoring of employees; may need a legal/HR basis

open_questions.question: Can users hide their last-online time?

options.changes: Feature shows little until users opt in
Criterion 3 removed; stronger privacy justification needed

open_questions.question: How long is the last-online time kept?

options.changes: Adds deletion job and its test

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version; privacy criteria blocked pending the owner.

actions_now: Write the draft spec with visibility, opt-out and retention as open questions blocking the criteria that depend on them, and escalate to the owner, because the criteria depend on privacy and people decisions the product role may not make. No line that shows the data starts until the owner answers.

specs.title: Exports contain the report's columns for reconciliation
sources: Owner request: "Exports must contain every column of the report, so finance can reconcile."
Decision dl-009: "Personal emails never leave the system in any export."
Current report columns, including Customer email
in_scope: Exports include every report column, with the Customer email column handled as the owner decides in Q1

criteria.text: Given a report, when it is exported, then the export contains every report column other than Customer email, with the same values as the report.
criteria.check: Test to write: compare export columns and values to the report, excluding Customer email.

criteria.text: Given a report with a Customer email column, when it is exported, then that column is handled as decided in Q1. BLOCKED by Q1.
criteria.check: Test to write per the answer (e.g. column absent, or present with values masked/replaced).

criteria.text: Given any export, when it is produced, then no personal email address appears anywhere in it (dl-009), unless Q1 changes dl-009.
criteria.check: Negative test: scan every exported cell for email addresses.

open_questions.question: The request (every column) contradicts dl-009 (no personal emails in any export). How is the Customer email column handled?

options.changes: Export is not literally every column; finance reconciles without email

options.option: Keep dl-009: replace emails with a non-personal customer identifier
options.changes: Finance can still match rows; needs a stable identifier

options.option: Owner revises dl-009 for this export
options.changes: Personal data leaves the system; new decision-log entry needed; criterion 3 changes

open_questions.waiting_for: owner (contradiction with a recorded privacy decision)

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version; email column blocked on the contradiction with dl-009.

actions_now: Write the draft spec citing both the request and dl-009, keep dl-009 in force in the criteria, and escalate the contradiction to the owner as an open question with options rather than choosing one; the non-email columns can proceed, the email column waits.

specs.title: Dark mode
sources: Owner request: "Add dark mode to the settings page, as a toggle that applies to the whole app."
in_scope: A dark mode toggle on the settings page
When on, the app's screens are shown in a dark theme (whether the invoice view and emails count as the app is Q1)
non_goals: New colour themes other than dark

criteria.text: Given the user is on the settings page, when they look for display options, then a dark mode toggle is present and shows its current state.
criteria.check: Manual step: open settings, expect the toggle with its current state; UI test.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is off, when the user turns it on, then every app screen in scope is shown in the dark theme without a reload.
criteria.check: UI test across the app's screens; manual step: toggle and visit each screen.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when the user turns it off, then the app returns to the current light appearance.
criteria.check: UI test; visual comparison with today's screens.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when text and controls are shown, then they meet the project's contrast requirement.
criteria.check: Accessibility check (contrast audit) on dark screens.

criteria.text: Given the user turned dark mode on, when they reload or sign in again, then the choice is kept as decided in Q2. BLOCKED by Q2.
criteria.check: Test to write per Q2.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when the user opens the printable invoice view or receives an email, then it is shown as decided in Q1. BLOCKED by Q1.
criteria.check: Manual step: print preview of an invoice and a sent email, expected per Q1.

expected_areas: Invoice view and email templates only if Q1 includes them

open_questions.question: Does "the whole app" include the printable invoice view and the email templates?

options.option: Invoice view on screen only, print stays light

options.changes: Email templates need dark variants; largest scope, separate line likely

open_questions.question: Where is the choice kept, and what is the default?

actions_now: Write the draft spec with the toggle and app-wide behaviour as criteria, and ask the owner whether the invoice view and email templates are part of "the whole app" and how the choice persists, instead of assuming either; send the draft for approval.

specs.title: Faster dashboard
sources: Owner request: "Make the dashboard faster."
Current dashboard: views Overview, Sales, Inventory, at today's measured load times
in_scope: Load and interaction time of the dashboard views named in Q2, to the target set in Q1
non_goals: Changing what data the views show
Performance of pages other than the dashboard

criteria.text: Given the baseline is measured for each view under the conditions in Q3, when the work starts, then the baseline is recorded in the spec's line.
criteria.check: Command/manual step: run the agreed measurement on each view and record the median and p95 times.

criteria.text: Given a view in scope (Q2), when it is loaded under the conditions in Q3, then the measured time meets the target in Q1. BLOCKED by Q1, Q2, Q3.
criteria.check: Repeatable performance measurement per view, compared to the target.

criteria.text: Given the faster dashboard, when each view is loaded, then it shows the same data as before the change.
criteria.check: Test to write: compare view data before and after for seeded data.

criteria.text: Given the data source is slow or fails, when a view loads, then it shows the current loading and error states rather than blank or stale data without notice.
criteria.check: Negative test with a delayed/failed data source.

open_questions.question: How fast is fast enough?

options.option: An absolute target (e.g. each view loads in under N seconds at p95)
options.changes: Clear pass/fail; N must be chosen

options.option: A relative target (e.g. X% faster than the baseline)

open_questions.question: Which views are in scope?

options.option: Only the views users find slow (which?)

open_questions.question: Under what conditions is speed measured (first load or repeat, data volume, network, which metric: time to first content or fully loaded)?

options.option: Production-like data volume, first load, fully loaded

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version; target blocked pending the owner.

actions_now: Write a draft spec that does not invent a speed target, and escalate to the owner because the goal is unclear: ask for the target, the views and the measurement conditions. Measuring the baseline (criterion 1) can go ahead meanwhile; the work against the target waits.

specs.title: CSV export on the reports page
sources: Owner request: "Add CSV export to the reports page, and a public REST API that partners can use to fetch the same reports." (export part)
Factory plan: export and partner API as two lines on two branches
Current reports page
in_scope: A user on the reports page can download the report they see as CSV
non_goals: The partner REST API (separate spec and line)

criteria.text: Given the reports page shows a report, when the user chooses Export CSV, then a CSV file downloads with the report's columns as the header row, in the page's order.
criteria.check: Test to write: header row equals the page's columns; manual step: export and open the file.

criteria.text: Given the report is filtered, when the user exports, then the file contains exactly the rows shown, with the same values.
criteria.check: Test to write: compare exported rows to the filtered table.

criteria.text: Given the filter matches no rows, when the user exports, then the behaviour decided in Q1 applies.
criteria.check: Negative test: empty result. BLOCKED by Q1.

criteria.text: Given a user who may not view the report, when they request the export directly, then it is refused as the page is refused today.
criteria.check: Negative test: unauthorized export request.

open_questions.question: What does an export with no matching rows produce?
Is there a size limit, and what happens above it?

specs.title: Partner REST API for reports
sources: Owner request: "Add CSV export to the reports page, and a public REST API that partners can use to fetch the same reports." (API part)
Factory plan: export and partner API as two lines on two branches
Current reports and their data
in_scope: An authorised partner can fetch the same reports over a public REST API
non_goals: The CSV export on the reports page (separate spec and line)

criteria.text: Given an authorised partner (per Q1, Q2), when they request a report they may see, then they receive the same rows and values the reports page shows for the same filter. BLOCKED by Q1, Q2.
criteria.check: API test: compare API response to the page's data for the same filter.

criteria.text: Given a request without valid credentials, when it reaches the API, then it is refused and no report data is returned. BLOCKED by Q1.
criteria.check: Negative test: missing and invalid credentials.

criteria.text: Given partner A, when they request data scoped to partner B or outside their permission, then it is refused. BLOCKED by Q2.
criteria.check: Negative test: tenant isolation.

criteria.text: Given a partner exceeds the request limit decided in Q3, when they send another request, then it is refused with a rate-limit response. BLOCKED by Q3.
criteria.check: Integration test at the limit.

criteria.text: Given an invalid filter or unknown report, when it is requested, then the API returns an error stating what is wrong and no data.
criteria.check: Negative test: invalid parameters.

open_questions.question: How do partners authenticate and who issues their access?

options.option: API keys issued by the owner's team

open_questions.question: Which reports and which data may each partner see? Do reports contain personal data that must not leave the system?

options.option: Only rows/reports scoped to that partner

open_questions.question: What request limits apply?
Who admits the API to go public to partners?

options.changes: Release waits on an Admit decision

actions_now: Write two separate draft specs, one per line and branch, each with its own numbered criteria and checks. The partner API's authentication, data exposure and going public go to the owner as security, privacy and admission questions; the export line can proceed independently once approved.
